title: Deep learning identifies mitral valve prolapse from echocardiogram videos
summary: DROID-MVP was trained on 1,043,893 echocardiogram videos (48,829 studies) from 16,902 cardiology patients at MGH and externally validated in 8,888 MGH primary care patients and 257 Brigham and Women's primary care patients. AUROC was 0.947 internally and 0.964 and 0.968 in the two external sets, with average precision of 0.651-0.774 at low prevalence. Predictions were associated with mitral regurgitation severity and later mitral valve repair or replacement; the study is retrospective.
ai_technology: DROID-MVP deep learning model classifying mitral valve prolapse from echocardiogram videos
